problem: Cities lacked fast, affordable measurement of residents' trust and sentiment; traditional polling is slow and expensive.

founders.name: Michael Simon
education: University of Michigan, BA Political Science
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch: pollster on Obama 2008 campaign; NYPD first hired him for a one-off study

competitors.name: Spidr Technologies
competitors.what: Service aimed at making Compstat more responsive

technical_complexity.rationale: Polling delivered through mobile ad networks with statistical weighting; mainly methodology and operations.

defensibility.rationale: Government relationships (NYPD pilot across 77 precincts) and survey data history; methodology copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zencity, a sentiment-tracking platform for local governments, acquired Elucd in March 2021 and said it would integrate Elucd's capabilities.

market_need_then: NYPD ran a six-month trial and was ready to roll the service out to 77 precincts (TechCrunch, Aug 2017); YC partner Michael Seibel called traditional polling wildly expensive; some investors doubted cities would pay a high price.

brand_strength.rationale: No source found about the brand itself; rated low-middle by default because nothing shows it drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Elucd began as an NYPD polling study run by an Obama-campaign pollster, passed YC in 2017 with a police-precinct rollout, and was acquired by Zencity in March 2021. The deal price and Elucd's total funding are not public, so whether it was a soft landing or a solid exit cannot be determined; a small govtech market and slow public-sector sales are plausible limits.
notes: Axios and BusinessWire returned 403 to fetches; the acquisition date (2021-03-04) is taken from search-result summaries of both and a StateScoop/MRWeb headline. A US$1M seed (YC and Omidyar Network) appears in a search summary citing Seedtable only, so is unverified and not recorded as a round. The website field in the directory is blank. TechCrunch gives no name origin. Spidr Technologies is the only dated competitor found. Completeness pass: the 1M seed (Jan 2018, Omidyar Network and Y Combinator) is listed by Seedtable and also reported by Government Technology (https://www.govtech.com/biz/elucd-a-community-pollster-for-police-raises-1m-seed-round.html) and by the founder's post on Medium; later rounds, if any, were not found.
